We also detect relatively weak Q-branch C2H2 (13.7µm) and HCN (14.02µm) molecular absorption in D1 (Appendix C).

all_quotes.quote: Although AGN emission is not clearly detected, there is evidence for the presence of an accreting SMBH in D1.
The exceptionally high covering factor of the dusty structure inhibits the direct detection of AGN emission.
The detected H2O and CO bands demonstrate a great potential for disentangling different components, specifically, four in the case of D1.

By comparing the observed molecular rovibrational bands with radiative transfer models, we find that D1 is a complex structure featuring an IR-bright embedded dusty core (i.e. torus), which is most likely connected to a highly turbulent environment.
The torus continuum level is indeed constrained by the observed H 2 O absorption band. This provides an observational limit to the contribution of the torus.

all_quotes.quote: We repeated the fitting process but including the 4.9-7.0 µm SED derived from the H2O and CO analysis (Fig. 4, left). The fractional contribution of the torus to the SED is lower (Ftorus 7µm ∼40%), and the derived torus bolometric luminosity is about nine times smaller.

The torus is very compact (diameter of ∼3 pc at 5 µm) and characterised by warm dust (∼ 370 K), giving an IR surface brightness of ∼3.6×108 L⊙/pc2. This result suggests the presence of a dust-obscured active galactic nucleus (AGN) in D1, which has an exceptionally high covering factor that prevents the direct detection of AGN emission.

all_quotes.loc: Appendix F: Residuals of the best-fit model of the molecular bands
all_quotes.quote: The latter are detected in the submm (e.g. Neufeld et al. 2000, 2002; Plume et al. 2004), and are not included in this model. As a consequence the fitted cold extended model for reproducing the relatively low-J lines of the CO band is overestimating the ∼R(4) to R(6) transitions.

all_quotes.loc: 4. Inner dusty structure modelling: Molecular bands as a tool for constraining the torus properties
all_quotes.quote: To build the 1-850 µm SED of D1, we used the entire NIRSpec and MRS spectra (resampled to ∼100 points), high angular resolution ALMA archival data (Appendix A), and lower angular resolution far-IR fluxes from Herschel.
